3 Chris applies a 90 N to a 65 kg bin. The bin will accelerate at:
[LV-MEDIA:{"images":[{"pack":"repo-science-batch26","id":"e60-image10"}]}]
questions.explanation: Assuming the stated 90 N is the net horizontal force, a=90/65≈1.38 m/s².

questions.prompt: 4 Power is the rate at which energy is supplied. What power is needed to supply 6000 J to lift a 15kg child 10 m up a vertical cliff face in 5 seconds?
questions.explanation: Power is the stated energy supplied divided by time: 6000/5=1200 J/s. Do not substitute the different ideal gravitational-energy estimate for the explicitly supplied input energy.

questions.prompt:
5 Look at the three pieces of ticker tape below, labelled A, B and C. Choose the answer that explains each piece correctly.
[LV-MEDIA:{"images":[{"pack":"repo-science-batch26","id":"e60-image11"}]}]
options: A: decelerating; B: constant speed; C: accelerating
A: constant speed; B: accelerating; C: decelerating
A: accelerating slowly; B: constant speed; C: decelerating
A: constant speed; B: accelerating slowly; C: accelerating faster
questions.explanation: Reading the tape in the intended direction: A has constant spacing, B spacing grows slowly, and C grows faster. D.

questions.prompt:
6  Two forces stretch a cable within a structure. Which of the following best describes the cable?
[LV-MEDIA:{"images":[{"pack":"repo-science-batch26","id":"e60-image12"}]}]
options: The cable is being stretched by gravity.
questions.explanation: A stretched structural cable is in tension.

questions.prompt: 7  When a door or window sticks it indicates that the structure:
options: has all of its forces balanced
has no forces acting on it
questions.explanation: Sticking doors/windows can indicate distortion and partial structural failure; other causes should be investigated in a real building.

questions.prompt: 8 An aircraft is flying in a straight line at constant altitude and at a constant speed. What can be said about the forces on the aircraft?
questions.explanation: Constant velocity means zero resultant force: the forces are balanced.

questions.prompt: 9  When standing, your legs are in:
questions.explanation: Compression is the intended principal axial load in the legs while standing.

questions.prompt: 10  Sandstone is a building material that is strong under:
questions.explanation: Sandstone is comparatively strong in compression and much weaker in tension; A is the intended relative-material-property answer, not literally zero tensile strength.

12  A cable was placed under tension until just before it broke. Which of the following diagrams best shows the cable just before it broke?
[LV-MEDIA:{"images":[{"pack":"repo-science-batch26","id":"e60-image13"}]}]
questions.explanation: A: tensile arrows point away from one another and the cable necks down near failure.

questions.prompt:
14 Which of the following is true about the diagram of the man and woman walking?
[LV-MEDIA:{"images":[{"pack":"repo-science-batch26","id":"e60-image15-crop-4b1bacda"}]}]
options: The woman is making marks in the ground because she is placing more force on the grass
The man is not making any marks on the ground because he is placing less force on the grass
The woman is making marks on the ground because her shoes have less area touching the ground
The man’s shoes are not making any marks on the ground because his have less area touching the ground
questions.explanation: C: smaller shoe contact area can increase pressure for comparable load, explaining the heel marks.

questions.prompt:
AA17 Which of the following is true about this diagram of a bridge?
[LV-MEDIA:{"images":[{"pack":"repo-science-batch26","id":"e60-page7-bridge-A-B-labels"}]}]
options: A shows compression; B shows tension
A shows tension; B shows compression
Both A and B show tension
Both A and B show compression
questions.explanation: A marks compression in the tower and B tension in the main cable in the original labelled bridge figure.

questions.prompt: 18 Leslie runs a race that starts and finishes at the same point. If the race was 1000 metres, what was Leslie’s displacement at the end of the race?
questions.explanation: Displacement is zero because the finish and start are the same position.

questions.prompt: 19 Leslie ran a second race but is unable to finish after spraining an ankle and 120 m east of the finish line. Given that the distance to be run in the race was 1000 m, and that the finish line was where the race started, the displacement of the racehorse is now:
questions.explanation: 120 m east of the start/finish point. “Racehorse” is a source copy-and-paste error; the described runner’s position is still specified.

questions.prompt: 21 Which of the following explains Newtons First Law?
options: The motion of an object will not change if all the forces acting on it are balanced
For every force there is an equal and opposite force
An object will accelerate in the direction of an unbalanced force
questions.explanation: A: motion remains unchanged when the resultant external force is zero.
